newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wool helps lift commodity index - Dresdner/NFF.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wool helps lift commodity index - Dresdner/NFF.

text.p: Higher wool prices helped lift the Dresdner Australia Ltd/National Farmers' Federation (NFF) international commodity index 0.6 percent in January from December, as measured in special drawing rights (SDR) terms.
Rural SDR prices in January were up 1.3 percent.
Wool price were up nearly 50 cents a kg, Dresdner and the NFF noted in a joint statment.

"While this improvement is at least partially due to lower offerings, the latest increase may indicate that the market has passed through the trough and is starting to strengthen," the statement said.
In Australian dollar terms, the index rose 1.7 percent.

The SDR index was now 4.6 percent above the year-ago level, although the appreciation of the Australian dollar in the last year left the index in local currency terms down 3.7 percent, the figures show.

A A$3 increase in the Australian Wheat Board export pool price estimate to A$188 a tonne last week was good news for wheat farmers in Australia, despite expectations of a record 23 million tonne crop this year, it said.
Non-rural commodities in SDR prices rose 0.3 percent in January from December and were up 5.9 percent from last January, figures show.
In Australian dollars, the non-rural index rose 1.4 percent over December.
Monthly average figures reveal energy prices were generally stronger up 1.8 percent in January from December in SDR terms.
The increase was underscored by firmer crude oil and LPG prices.
At the same time, metals prices increased marginally, led by nickel, copper and aluminium.
An exception was gold, which fell three percent.

Overall, the world economy remains supportive for commodity prices, with strong growth in the U.S. offsetting somewhat patchy recoveries in most G-7 economies, notably Japan and Germany, the statement said.
